term: has intellect (ST I q.14; Lean parameter `HasIntellect` of `GodHasIntellect`)
definition: Having intellect means intellectual cognition, distinguished from sense in ST I q.14 a.1 by its greater separation from matter. Cognition involves the form of what is known in the knower; divine cognition is not a created habit or quality. HasIntellect remains a primitive predicate of beings in GodHasIntellect and ClassicalAttributesSuffice.
note: ImmaterialIsIntellectualReading asserts that what is neither matter-form composite nor a component of anything has intellect. That strong antecedent is the case interpretation of the source's highest immateriality, not a definition of all intellect or a claim that sense cognition is intellectual. No species-of-knowledge semantics is enforced by the primitive predicate.
